To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HER2Δ 16 overexpression promotes tamoxifen-resistant and estrogen-independent breast cancer in vivo.
(1) HER2Δ16 promotes endocrine-resistant breast tumors; and (2) HER2ΔΔ16 suppresses microRNA-mediated BCL- 2 downregulation and promotes tamoxifen-induced resistance of breast tumors.
HER2Δ-16 expression results in endocrine-resistant breast tumors and in these tumors, tamoxifen-induced expression of BCL- 2 is mediated by miR-15/16 suppression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of tamoxifen resistance in HER2/ER co-expressing breast cancers.
the molecular mechanism of endocrine resistance in ER-positive breast cancer, which is the most commonly diagnosed and most prevalent form of breast cancer.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies to treat endocrine-resistant breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HER2Δ-16 expression in MCF-7 cells results in tamoxifen resistance through BCL-2 upregulation and miR-15/16 suppression.
the oncogenic isoform HER2Δ16 promotes endocrine-resistant human ERα/HER2-positive breast tumors through upregulation BCL-2 mediated by suppression of miR15/16.
the HER2Δ16 oncogene promotes tamoxifen-resistant endocrine therapy in ER-positive breast tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

HER2Δ 16 expression is associated with endocrine resistance in ER+/HER2-positive breast tumors, and that the resistance is due to the suppression of miR15/16 expression and the upregulation of the anti-apoptotic protein Bcl-2, which is a target of miR15a/16.
the oncogenic isoform HER2Δ16 is overexpressed in 30% of ER positive breast tumors and that it promotes resistance to tamoxifin and fulvestrant through the induction of BCL-1.

HER2Δ6 is a novel therapeutic target for endocrine resistance of ERα-positive breast tumors, and that the mechanism of HER2δ6 therapeutic evasion involves tamoxifen-induced activation of BCL- 2 and suppression of microRNA-15a/ 16, which can be targeted by combination therapy with ABT-737 and microRNAs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HER2Δ15/16, which is overexpressed in 30% of ERα-positive breast tumors, can promote tamoxifen resistance through suppression of miR15/16 and upregulation of anti-apoptotic protein BCL-2.
the HER2Δ16 isoform is a major oncogenic factor in endocrine-resistant breast tumors, and it is not the wild-type HER2 protein that is expressed in the majority of breast tumors.
HER2Δ 16 expression promotes tamoxifen-resistance of ER-positive breast cancer cells and that this resistance is mediated by suppression of miR15a/16.
